emily (support): Heads up: AcmeHealth ticket #4521 — customers report p99 latency spike after we rolled the int8 calibration last night. Seeing ~3-4x p99 on long-form generation. Escalating to eng.

tony (oncall): On it. Can you attach a sample request, the trace, and the quant profile id? Also which model variant?

emily (support): Sample and traces here: https://redwood.internal/trace/4521 and request payload (redacted). Model = redwood-v2-medium-int8-calib-2026-03-15. Quant profile id = qp-20260315-aggr.

megan (eng-ml): Got it. Was calibration run with any experimental flags (fp8, per-layer-bias-correct, aggressive)? Also whats the KV cache hit rate during the spike window?

emily (support): Ops used `--mode=aggressive` for the calibration. KV cache hit reported ~10% during the spike. Customer said most requests are long summaries (~1200 tokens).

dan (eng-runtime): Looking at the traces — p99 spikes correlate with seq_len > 1k. I'm seeing a large increase in dequant/quant ops in attention path for those requests. Suspect extra dequant hops introduced by profile causing slower kernels for long sequences.

megan (eng-ml): That matches my hypothesis. Aggressive profile may have enabled per-layer scaling that the runtime currently handles with an inefficient code path for long attention. We should instrument count of dequant ops and kernel types.

emily (support): Repro steps from customer (condensed):
1) 24 concurrent sessions
2) 80 req/min per session
3) input ~1000-1400 tokens, generate ~800 tokens
They reproduced locally with our stress harness.

lee (acme-customer): We rolled back the profile to fp16 last night and p99 returned to baseline. We prefer a fix that keeps int8 quality but without the latency regression.

dan (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation we can do now: enable routing policy that sends long sequences to fp16 variant. Add a canary at 5% for affected tenants while we investigate full fix. Example route rule:

```
if request.seq_len > 800 or request.estimated_tokens > 700:
  route -> redwood-v2-medium-fp16
else:
  route -> redwood-v2-medium-int8-calib-2026-03-15
```

tony (oncall): Ops will roll the canary. Command I'm using: `rictl route create --name acme-longseq-canary --percent 5 --condition "seq_len>800" --target redwood-v2-medium-fp16`

ops-bot: deploy job 98432 started by tony (oncall) — canary rule applying to traffic group acme-health.

emily (support): Canary live. Monitoring p50/p95/p99 for AcmeHealth. Will report back in 15m windows.

12m later — emily (support): Early results: p99 for AcmeHealth dropped ~70% after canary started. p95 stable. Customer confirmed improved experience.

megan (eng-ml): For a permanent fix we should:
- Re-run calibration with conservative flags: `--mode=standard --per-layer-bias-correct=false`
- Increase calibration sample count: `--calib-samples=2000` and `--minibatch=8`
- Validate latency profile across seq buckets (<=256, 256-800, >800)
I'll kick off a calibration job tonight and run the latency eval.

dan (eng-runtime): Also adding runtime metrics to detect this class of issue automatically: `quant_dequant_ops_count`, `int8_slow_path_invocations`, and `kv_cache_hit_ratio` per model. We'll surface these as alarms when p95/p99 diverge from expected baseline.

megan (eng-ml): After re-calibration we should do an A/B rollout: 5% → 20% → 50% with continuous p99 guardrails. If we see a regression, automatic rollback triggers.

emily (support): Customer updated: they appreciate the rapid mitigation and want ETA for permanent fix.

megan (eng-ml): ETA: calibration jobs + offline latency validation + safe rollout ~48 hours. I will post job id and results in this thread when done.

dan (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for eng-runtime: add detection rule in routing layer to autodetect sustained seq_len skew and apply fallback routing policy automatically (configurable per-tenant).

emily (support): I'll update ticket #4521 with the canary details and the 48h timeline. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

lee (acme-customer): Thanks all — please keep us posted. Our PM wants a short postmortem once fix is live.

emily (support): Will schedule a short RCA and notify after rollout.

---
Notes for RCA:
- Suspected cause: aggressive int8 calibration introduced per-layer quant params that cause dequant/quant op expansion on long-attention kernels, leading to slower kernel selection and p99 regression for long-sequence workloads.
- Immediate mitigation: routing-based fallback to fp16 for long sequences (canaryed at 5%).
- Permanent path: conservative re-calibration + increased samples + runtime telemetry + guarded rollout.

will follow up with job ids and metrics.
